item.title: Desert masquerades: Dubai’s high-fashion take on Halloween nights
item.description: Dubai is transforming Halloween into a high-fashion spectacle, blending luxury with fantasy. Rooftop parties, masquerade dinners, and influencer-hosted events are now curated experiences focused on style and social media. This evolution showcases Dubai's status as a global influencer hub, reinventing the holiday beyond costumes and candy into a lifestyle showcase.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: 1,600-year-old Roman wine factory discovered beneath ancient castle
item.description: Archaeologists in Turkey unearthed a 1,600-year-old Roman wine production site near Kahta Castle. The remarkably preserved complex, spanning 37 acres, features grape-crushing installations and cisterns, indicating large-scale industrial winemaking. This discovery offers insights into the thriving local economies and agricultural sophistication of the late Roman period in remote mountain regions.

item.title: WWI soldiers’ letters found in a bottle on Australian beach: What’s written inside
item.description: A family's beach clean-up in Western Australia unearthed a century-old message in a bottle. Two Australian WWI soldiers, Privates Malcolm Neville and William Harley, penned letters aboard the HMAT A70 Ballarat in 1916, expressing optimism before heading to the Western Front. Their messages, remarkably preserved, have now connected their descendants, offering a poignant glimpse into the past.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: No more bumpy flights: How Emirates is using artificial intelligence to make turbulence a thing of the past
item.description: Emirates is using advanced tech to make flights smoother and safer. By combining AI, real-time weather data, and global turbulence tracking tools, the airline has cut down on severe turbulence incidents and improved comfort for passengers and crew. The new system also helps pilots plan calmer routes while sharing valuable data with the wider aviation industry.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Will obliterate Afghan Taliban & push them back to caves: Pakistan
Nina Lin causes outrage on Pokimane stream with boyfriend rules amid sexual assault controversy
item.description: A viral mukbang clip features streamer Nina Lin detailing extreme demands for an ideal partner, including complete obedience and financial control. Her "slave-like" requirements shocked viewers, especially following recent Twitch ban allegations. Fellow streamers Pokimane and iGumdrop's supportive reactions to Lin's controversial preferences have further fueled online debate about her behavior.
item.dc:creator: Sehjal Gupta

item.title: Indian-origin Balraj Singh Basra sentenced to life in Canada for 2022 gangwar murder of Vishal Walia
item.description: Three men have been sentenced for the 2022 murder of gangster Vishal Walia. Iqbal Kang received 17 years for conspiracy, Deandre Baptiste life without parole for 17 years for second-degree murder, and Balraj Basra life without parole for 25 years for first-degree murder and arson. Justice Milman described the killing as an execution.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: U.S. Vice President JD Vance comments on Hasan Piker’s dog collar controversy
item.description: US Vice President JD Vance has entered the "Collargate" debate surrounding Twitch streamer Hasan Piker, referencing the controversy over his dog's electronic collar on a podcast. Vance's remarks, linking animal welfare to broader empathy, have sparked discussions about online culture's reach into mainstream politics, highlighting the growing intersection of influencers and national discourse.
item.dc:creator: Global Sports Desk

item.title: UAE Central Bank cuts interest rate to 3.90%; lowest since 2022, consumers to see cheaper loans and mortgages
item.description: The UAE Central Bank has lowered its base rate on overnight deposits by 25 basis points to 3.90%, following the US Federal Reserve’s latest rate cut. This marks the UAE’s second reduction this year and its lowest level since 2022. The move aims to ease borrowing costs, support growth, and maintain stability under the dollar peg.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Indian American groups condemn Zohran Mamdani’s ‘Hinduphobic’ remarks as acts of bigotry and bias
item.description: A coalition of Indian American and Hindu diaspora groups has condemned New York City mayoral candidate Zohran Mamdani for alleged "Hinduphobic actions and statements." The organizations accused Mamdani of promoting bigotry and bias, citing his rhetoric on issues like the CAA and his response to temple attacks. They questioned his ability to represent the Hindu community in good faith.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Florida bans H-1B in higher education: 'Why do we need someone from China to talk about public policy,' asks Gov Ron DeSantis
item.description: Florida Governor Ron DeSantis has directed the state's Board of Governors to cease the use of H-1B visas in colleges and universities. He asserted that these positions can and should be filled by American workers, questioning the necessity of foreign hires for roles like assistant professors and coaches. According to USCIS data, as of June 30, 2025, there are 78 H-1B employers and 677 beneficiaries in Florida's higher education sector.

item.title: Did QuarterJade and Masayoshi split? Streamer finally responds to breakup speculation live on Twitch
item.description: Twitch stars QuarterJade and Masayoshi are very much together, dispelling breakup rumors. QuarterJade confirmed their status, explaining a past two-week break helped them communicate better during arguments. This period of space, even including a trip to Vegas, ultimately strengthened their relationship, as evidenced by recent public appearances and social media clips.
item.dc:creator: Sehjal Gupta

item.title: UAE-Russia: Air Arabia announces weekly direct flights from Ras Al Khaimah to Yekaterinburg
item.description: Air Arabia has launched its first weekly non-stop flight between Ras Al Khaimah and Yekaterinburg, Russia, marking another step in its network expansion. The new route complements existing flights to Moscow and reflects the airline’s strategy to boost UAE–Russia connectivity, offering passengers affordable fares, modern aircraft, and enhanced onboard experiences through its ‘SkyTime’ and ‘SkyCafe’ services.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: UAE finalises new sugar-tax rates for sweetened drinks, sets 0% rate for artificial sweeteners
item.description: The UAE has finalised plans to introduce a tiered volumetric tax on sweetened drinks from 1 January 2026, replacing the flat 50 per cent rate. Announced earlier this year and confirmed in October, the policy links tax to sugar content per 100 ml. Authorities say the update gives producers and retailers ample time to reformulate products and ensure compliance.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Zoharan Mamdani’s ‘Flagrant’ moment: Andrew Schulz roasts London as Mamdani recalls his family’s return to Uganda
item.description: New York City mayoral candidate Zohran Mamdani shared his family's exile from Uganda on the Flagrant podcast. Host Andrew Schulz humorously critiqued London's housing conditions during Mamdani's story of seeking refuge there before returning to Uganda. The exchange highlighted the podcast's blend of serious topics with comedic commentary.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: UAE: Indian embassy announces three new Indian passport designs for residents with advanced security features
item.description: Indian expats in the UAE are now navigating a unique situation with three different Indian passport designs in circulation: older booklets, machine-readable versions, and the new chip-enabled e-passports. While all remain valid until expiry, this transition necessitates awareness of potential differences in renewal fees, travel formalities, and verification processes for the large Indian diaspora.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Hurricane Melissa: 25 dead in Haiti floods; river bursts banks, homes swept away
item.description: Hurricane Melissa's devastating passage through the Caribbean has resulted in at least 25 deaths in Petit-Goave, Haiti, due to severe flooding from the La Digue river. The catastrophic Category 5 storm also caused widespread destruction in Jamaica and Cuba, leaving thousands homeless and without power.
